title: Log provenance ledger and correlation reconciliation
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Logs arriving from multiple ingestion paths (edge agents, sidecars, batch uploads, replay) lack a stable, canonical correlation key across systems. This creates duplicate records, broken joins between traces and logs, and incorrect attribution in incident dashboards. Existing solutions add ad-hoc correlation fields in individual services, which still diverge and make cross-system debugging brittle.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, append-only provenance ledger plus reconciliation pipeline that produces a canonical correlation map (canonical_corr_id) for every logical event. The system should normalize incoming correlation identifiers, deduplicate multi-path arrivals, attach provenance metadata (source, ingestion_time, original_correlation_ids), and emit enriched records back to Loki/ELK and the tracing platform so dashboards and trace-log joins are reliable.

Success criteria: Reduction in trace-log join failures, elimination of duplicate search hits caused by duplicate events, measurable decrease in mean time to correlate logs to spans for production incidents, and near-zero additional latency for the hot path.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical_corr_id is generated or resolved for >=99.5% of new incoming log events within the ingestion window
Duplicate arrivals (same logical event via multiple ingestion routes) are deduplicated downstream with <=1% false positives at peak traffic
Enriched logs written to Loki and ELK contain provenance fields: canonical_corr_id, provenance_sources, provenance_first_seen, provenance_sequence
Trace/log join dashboards show a >=50% reduction in unmatched logs for traced requests during canary tenants
End-to-end latency overhead on the ingest path (median) remains <5ms additional per log event in steady-state
tasks: Design schema for provenance ledger (keys, versioning, compaction window)
Implement lightweight ledger service (append-only, idempotent writes, sequence watermarking)
Build reconciliation worker that coalesces multiple incoming identifiers into canonical_corr_id
Enrichment client in log-forwarders to attach canonical_corr_id before writing to sinks
Integrate reconciler outputs with Loki label enrichment and ELK ingest pipeline (Logstash/Beats)
Add tracing hook to propagate canonical_corr_id into span attributes when available
Backfill tool to reconcile last 30 days of logs for a selected tenant
Instrumentation and Grafana dashboards for reconciliation rate, lag, dedupe rate, false positives
Load and chaos testing on non-prod with production-like traffic
Run canary with 3 pilot tenants and collect SLA/quality metrics
implementation_steps: Phase 1: Design & PoC (2 weeks) - define ledger schema, unique key derivation rules, and a reconciliation algorithm that uses time-windowed coalescing and stable heuristics (primary: trace_id/span_id/timestamp; secondary: request_id/user_agent/host)

Phase 2: Core Ledger Service (3 weeks) - append-only API, idempotent write via dedupe_key, persistent storage in DynamoDB/Spanner with compacted indexes and TTLs, sequence watermark support for safe compaction
Phase 3: Reconciler Workers (2 weeks) - stream consumer off the ingest Kafka topic, reconcile correlated ids, emit canonical mapping events to a dedicated topic and to a reconciliation-state store

Phase 4: Enrichment & Sink Integration (2 weeks) - implement lightweight enrichment layer in the log-forwarder sidecar to query reconciliation state (cache + fallback) and attach canonical_corr_id; modify Loki pipeline to accept label canonical_corr_id and update ELK ingest processors to set field
Phase 5: Tracing Hook & Dashboards (1 week) - add SDK hook to set span attribute 'redwood.canonical_corr_id' when present; build observability dashboards and alerts
Phase 6: Backfill & Canary (2 weeks) - backfill recent history for pilot tenants; run canary, collect metrics, iterate on heuristics
Phase 7: Rollout (ongoing) - expand tenant coverage, adjust compaction/retention and operational runbooks
testing_plan: Unit tests for ledger idempotency and compaction logic
Integration tests: synthetic multi-path event generation to ensure reconciliation maps properly across 3+ ingestion routes
Performance tests: peak ingestion simulation (2x expected peak) to validate latency and dedupe stability
Chaos tests: partial consumer failures and out-of-order replay to validate reconcilers are eventually consistent
Validation tests: trace-log join tooling that asserts reconciliation improves join rates vs baseline
rollout_plan: Create feature-flag controlled enrichment so tenants opt-in to canonical enrichment
Canary cohort: 3 low-latency pilot tenants for 72 hours, monitor reconciliation_rate, dedupe_rate, join_success_rate
Progressively enable for 10% of tenants, then 50%, then 100% with automated rollback criteria
Rollback criteria: >2% increase in end-to-end payload latency, >1% increase in lost logs, or significant increase in false dedupes detected by sampling
Post-rollout: schedule a 2-week review to tune heuristics and compaction windows
metrics: reconciliation_rate: fraction of events with canonical_corr_id attached
reconciliation_lag_ms: median and p95 time between first_seen and canonical mapping emission
dedupe_rate: fraction of events suppressed by reconciler
trace_log_join_success_rate: fraction of spans with at least one matched log within time window
false_positive_rate: sampled manual audit of deduped events marked as distinct
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased read latency from reconciliation state store on hot path. Mitigation: local LRU cache, bloom-filter pre-check, and async enrichment with streaming patch if miss
Risk: Incorrect coalescing leading to false dedupes. Mitigation: conservative default heuristics, maintain provenance history and allow undo via rehydrate tool
Risk: Storage cost explosion for provenance metadata. Mitigation: compacted TTL windows, tiered retention (hot 7d, warm 30d, cold 90d), and periodic compaction jobs
Risk: Cross-tenant contamination due to key collisions. Mitigation: tenant-scoped ledger namespaces and strict validation in write path
notes: We should coordinate with Platform Security before enabling enrichment that exposes any user-provided IDs in canonical_corr_id fields
Consider a reversible hash function for canonical_corr_id if customers prefer non-raw identifiers
Early telemetry suggests roughly 12% of production incidents had missing log-to-trace links that this could resolve
